channel.title: NBC Sports Fantasy Football News
channel.description: Latest player news and analysis for fantasy football from NBC Sports.

item.title: Brandon Aiyuk’s agent, Drew Rosenhaus, said talks between him and the 49ers are “to be continued.”
item.description: Aiyuk and Rosenhaus met with the 49ers’ “big bosses” today to discuss an amicable solution to their multi-year conflict. Aiyuk seeks reinstatement, but under league rules, heowes the 49ers roughly $13 million in bonus forfeiture. The two sides met today, but evidently, things were not resolved. The saga continues. Stay tuned.-Nic Bodiford

item.title: Kenny Gainwell (hip) was removed from the injury report and will play in Week 9 against the Bears.
item.description: Gainwell has been a little more involved in recent weeks, and coach Todd Bowles recently told reporters that they are getting closer to the 1A/1B usage that they envisioned when they signed him. Gainwell will again play sidekick to Bucky Irving this week.-Nic Bodiford

item.title: Tristan Wirfs (toe) was removed from the injury report and will play in Week 9 against the Bears.
item.description: The Buccaneers will have their starting left tackle on hand when they take on the Bears’ ascending defensive line in Week 9. Wirfs is one of the best offensive tackles in football. Having him on the field is always a plus for Baker Mayfield.-Nic Bodiford

item.title: George Pickens (hamstring) is questionable to play in Week 9 against the Colts.
item.description: Earlier today, Cowboys owner Jerry Jones said he is “hopeful” that Pickens will be available for this weekend’s game against the Colts. Pickens ended up being limited in practice all week and appears to be truly questionable to play. If active, he is a WR2 against a beatable Colts defense.-Nic Bodiford

item.title: Rashee Rice (hamstring/knee) is not on the Chiefs’ final injury report and will play in Week 9 against the Jets.
item.description: Rice posted a 7/53/1 receiving line against the Broncos last week. He got in a limited session on Wednesday before upgrading to full on Thursday. He seems to be recovering effectively from his summer knee procedure and in-season hamstring injury. Rice is a borderline WR1/2 for this weekend’s game against the Jets.-Nic Bodiford

item.title: Travis Kelce (ankle) is not on the Chiefs’ final injury report and will play in Week 9 against the Jets.
item.description: Kelce caught 5-of-7 targets for 67 yards, playing through the ankle injury last week against the Broncos, looking slightly hobbled. Kelce was limited to begin the week, but got in two full practices over the last two days. He remains firmly in the TE1 tier for Week 9 against the Jets.-Nic Bodiford

item.title: Christian Darrisaw (shoulder) practiced in full on Friday.
item.description: Darrisaw is now firmly on track to play in Week 9’s Monday Night Football game against the Bills, who field a tough, talented defensive line. Having Darrisaw on the field will be helpful for pocket passer Carson Wentz.-Nic Bodiford

item.title: NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport reports that “the plan” is for Quenton Nelson to avoid injured reserve after undergoing a procedure to remove cartilage fragments from his knee.
item.description: If the Seahawks were to place Nelson on short-term injured reserve, he would be required to miss at least four games. The Seahawks face the Cardinals this week, the Raiders next and then go on bye. Nelson could have a chance to play in Week 12 against the 49ers. His availability that week will likely just come down to how the recovery is going. His loss is unfortunate.-Nic Bodiford

item.title: Michael Wilson (NIR-rest/ribs) is not on the final injury report for Week 9 against the Seahawks.
item.description: Wilson caught 8-of-15 targets for 111 yards and a touchdown in the Cardinals’ Week 8 win over the Cowboys while playing through a pair of broken ribs. The Cardinals kept him limited all week. He should be good to go for WR2 duties against the Seahawks’ elite defense this week.-Nic Bodiford

item.title: Commanders ruled out Treylon Burks (foot) for Week 9 against the Rams.
item.description: The Commanders’ wide receiver corps continues to lose players. Burks and Dyami Brown (calf) will both be sidelined this weekend, leaving Stefon Diggs, Antonio Williams and Chig Okonkwo to operate as the top pass catchers.-Nic Bodiford
